chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Aban, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, Allah has assigned four thousand angels to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), disheveled and covered with dust. They weep for him from the rising of dawn until the sun declines. When the sun declines, four thousand angels descend and four thousand ascend. They continue weeping for him until dawn rises. They bear witness for whoever visits him, accompany him with loyalty to his family, visit him if he becomes ill, and offer prayers for him when he dies.
ai.seo_question: What role do angels play in honoring the grave of Imam al-Husayn and his visitors?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh highlights the cosmic significance of Karbala by describing a perpetual rotation of eight thousand angels weeping at Imam al-Husayn’s grave, symbolizing the eternal nature of his sacrifice. This continuous mourning serves as a spiritual mechanism where angels actively intercede for pilgrims, testifying to their sincerity, accompanying them home, and praying for them at death, thereby linking the act of ziyarah to divine reward and protection.
